basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 17.' and it opens '(Vers. 17.) Et abiit inde Isaac, et venit in vallem Gerarum, et habitavit ibi. Pro valle,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 17.) Et abiit inde Isaac, et venit in vallem Gerarum, et habitavit ibi. Pro valle, torrentem habet in Hebraeo. Neque enim Isaac postquam magnificatus est, habitare poterat in valle. Habitavit autem in torrente, de quo scriptum est: De torrente in via bibet (Psalm. CIX, 7). De quo etiam Elias tempore famis bibit. Sed quia Elias non erat perfectus, ut Christus: ideo ei torrens ille aruit (III Reg. XVII, 7). Dominus vero noster, etiam in torrente traditus est: dedicans regenerationem nostram et Baptismi sacramentum.
